# OTA drift model and reconcile policy

The correct model is not 鈥淥TA wipes all debloat state鈥?

## Package enabled state
Android stores per-user package enabled state in PackageManager settings under `/data`.
However, AOSP's package installation/update path explicitly contains logic that can implicitly
enable a system package on upgrade unless the installer requests
`applicationEnabledSettingPersistent`.

Therefore:
- a normal reboot should preserve `disabled-user`;
- an OTA does not inherently format `/data`;
- a system-package update MAY reset a disabled system package to DEFAULT;
- newly added/renamed packages obviously have no prior desired state.

UAD-ng itself exposes package-state snapshots to restore choices after OTA/major OEM upgrades.

## AppOps
AOSP AppOps removes package ops on real package removal, not a normal replacement update.
On package replacement it refreshes attributions. Therefore normal third-party app updates
usually do not imply that `RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND=ignore` disappears.

## DeviceIdle whitelist
The user whitelist is persisted in `/data/system/deviceidle.xml`.
Nevertheless, this HONOR device has already shown OEM/app policy re-adding Alipay and other
packages after restart. Treat whitelist as persistent state with possible OEM policy drift.

## Reconcile policy
- system package, same versionCode: reapply desired disable automatically;
- system package, changed versionCode: report/review role first, then reapply;
- third-party Reduced: reapply AppOps if missing;
- whitelist desired absent: enforce once; if a known drift package is re-added, report owner
  rather than installing an infinite boot-time fight loop;
- new package after OTA: report as NEW_AFTER_OTA and classify separately.
